    Camera file to a picture

    What happensA camera raw is not a picture. It is the sensor’s own measurement, and beside it, in the same file, sits the photograph the camera made from that measurement. That photograph is what comes out here. As JPG its bytes are copied across untouched — nothing is redrawn and no pixel changes — and the only thing that may be added is a 36-byte mark saying which way up it goes. How much of the full picture you are getting is measured from the file and said before you tap. Nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves this phone.
    Choose a file first.

    Unlock a PDF

    What happensYou type the password of your own locked PDF once. A copy is made that opens without it; your original stays locked. Or tick the box to lock the copy with a NEW password instead. The passwords stay on this phone and are forgotten as soon as the copy is made.
    Bank statement? What the bank itself says the password is

      To change a weak or shared password: the copy opens only with the new one (AES-256, the strongest PDF lock). Write it down; nobody can recover it.
      Choose a file first. The first unlock downloads a 7 MB tool once; your file is never sent anywhere.
      Make it A4, smaller in KB, its tables into Excel… straight away, without choosing the file again.

      Tables to Excel

      What happensEvery table in the PDF becomes a sheet in one Excel file. A table that runs over many pages becomes one sheet, with its heading once. Amounts become numbers you can add up (1,23,456.78 stays in the Indian style), dates become dates, and cheque numbers keep their zeros. Words that are not in a table go on a last sheet, so nothing is lost. Every cell is checked against the PDF before you get the file. After it, each table can also be saved as a CSV.
      Draw the table yourself

      When the Excel file misses a table, joins two tables into one, or puts words in the wrong column: drag a box round the table on each page, then tap where each column ends. Only what is inside your boxes becomes the table, cut at your lines. Everything else goes on the last sheet, so nothing is lost.

      Choose the PDF first

      Choose a file first. The first time downloads a 14 MB tool once; your file is never sent anywhere. A scanned page is read by text recognition (about 7 MB more, the first time only), and every number it was unsure of is marked yellow.
      Also as CSV, for Google Sheets (made from the same checked cells; one file per table). Tally imports the Excel file, not a CSV, and its bank-statement import takes only the bank's own download, never one made from a PDF:

        PDF to Word

        What happensThe PDF is rebuilt as a Word file you can edit: headings, paragraphs, tables and pictures come out in the same places, so it looks like the PDF rather than like a wall of text. This is the very same converter the laptop uses, carried into this page, so the Word file is the same file. Your PDF is not changed and never leaves this phone. The first time, a 36 MB tool is downloaded once – you are told how long the job will take, and you tap again to start it or walk away.
        Choose a file first. A scanned page is a picture: its pictures come across, but the words in them cannot be edited.

          Word to PDF

          What happensThe Word file is drawn out page by page here on the phone, checked word by word against the file itself, and then your phone’s own “Save as PDF” makes the PDF. Your file is not changed and nothing leaves the phone. Two limits, measured on eight real forms rather than guessed: the page breaks may not fall exactly where Word puts them, and a header or footer that Word repeats on every page is drawn once, at the top of its section. There is no Word on a phone, so what is checked is that every word came across – not where it landed.
          Choose a file first.

            Form for stamp paper

            What happensChoose a Word file that holds a form or affidavit set for stamp paper. Each section of it (a form set usually puts each annexure on its own page-run) becomes its own Word file, one per stamp paper. In each file the empty lines at the top are replaced by one blank space as tall as the stamp, so the first words start below the stamp. Every word, every ____ blank and every table stays exactly as you typed it; nothing is filled in, and your own file is not changed. Which paper each part is for (e-stamp or bond paper) is read from that part’s own words. If a part is longer than the space under the stamp, it runs on to a second plain page, and it says so. Everything happens here on this phone; the small tool (about 6 MB) downloads once.
            The stamp heights are a guess, not an official size (15 cm for an e-stamp paper, 12 cm for bond paper, measured from the top edge of the paper): no government page states one. Measure your own paper from its top edge to just below the stamp and type it in the box; that number is then used for every part.

                Rescue a broken file

                What happensA file that will not open is usually only partly broken: a download that stopped, a phone that switched off while saving. Everything still readable is taken out and put back together as a new copy, then read back to check it. Your original is not changed. First it says what the file really is: a "broken" Word file is often a web page saved with the wrong name, and then there is nothing to repair.
                Choose a file first. The first repair downloads a 9 MB tool once; your file is never sent anywhere.
                  Fit it to A4, shrink it, its tables into Excel… without choosing the file again.

                  Voice note to MP3

                  What happensA WhatsApp voice note is not an MP3: it is Opus, which many websites, older players and upload forms refuse. The sound is read out of your recording and written again as an MP3, then played back and compared with the original — how long it is, how loud it is, where its loud and quiet parts fall, and, from the lowest notes to the highest, whether any of the sound is gone. If a smaller MP3 lost some sound, it is made again at the recording's full quality by itself. If sound is still missing, nothing is saved, it says exactly what is missing, and a Save it anyway button lets you keep it knowing that. Your original is not touched. An MP3 is often bigger than the voice note it came from; that is the format, not a fault.

                  Write down the words reads the recording and writes what was said into a .txt beside it, in English or Hindi, without sending it anywhere. The first time, it downloads about 240 MB — do that on wi-fi. It is slow: it will tell you roughly how long before it starts, and you can stop there. Two checks run first and cost nothing: if the recording is silent, or if there is sound but no voice in it, nothing is written at all — asked about a hum, these engines invent words.
                  Choose a recording first. The first one downloads a 165 KB MP3 writer once; your recording is never sent anywhere.

                    Make a video fit a size

                    What happensType the most the video may be, in MB (a limit of 16 MB is read as 16,000,000 bytes, the smaller of the two ways MB is counted, so it always fits). The video is read on this phone, and from its length a plan is made: how many bits a second the picture and the sound may use. If that is too few for the picture at its size, the picture is made smaller (1080 lines to 720, 540...) rather than blocky; if it is still too few, it plays fewer frames a second. Your phone’s own video encoder then makes a new MP4 (H.264 picture, AAC sound: what every phone, WhatsApp and website plays). A phone’s encoder can land a little over what it is asked, so the size is checked, and if it is over it is made again at 90%, then 80%. It is never saved over the size. Then the new video is read back: its length, its picture size and whether it still has sound. A video too long to fit at all is refused, with how much of it would fit. The first time, it downloads a 0.7 MB video tool; your video is never sent anywhere. Your original is not touched.
                    Choose a video, then type the size it must fit.

                      Summarise

                      What happensEvery sentence in the file is read, and the ones the rest of the file keeps coming back to are picked out: one line, about one page, or a few from each chapter. They are the file’s own sentences, word for word, never rewritten, and each carries the page it is on (in a Word file, its paragraph number), so you can go and read round it. Tables, page numbers, running headers, picture captions and the list of references are left out. Nothing is sent anywhere and no AI writes anything: a small AI model was tried for this on real admission notices and it reversed a fact, so it is not used.
                      Choose a file first. A PDF uses the page reader the other PDF tools here use, downloaded once.

                      Edit by typing

                      What happensType the change in plain words. Every paragraph it would touch is shown before and after, and nothing is kept until you tap Keep this change; the file you chose is never changed, a new copy is saved. Changes add up: after a Keep, the next change is made on the edited copy, so the newest copy holds every change you kept, and Undo the last change steps back one. There is no AI in this: it knows a fixed list of changes, and if one word of what you typed is not understood, nothing is done, rather than half of it. A small AI model was tried for this and turned “red and bold” into bold only, so it is not used. A Word file (.docx) only: a PDF cannot be changed like this, so turn it into Word first with PDF to Word.

                      What you can type
                        Or say it, in English or Hindi

                        Tap the microphone and say the change, like “make fees bold”. It is turned into words on this phone (the first time it downloads a speech tool and says how long it will take). The command is put in the box above so you can read it; nothing changes until you tap Show the change and then Keep this change. If a word is not understood, nothing is done.

                        Choose a Word file, then type what to change.

                        Fix a problem

                        What happensGive it the PDF or Word file that is giving trouble. It is checked for every problem this page knows how to find – damaged, locked, cut off part-way, not A4, gaps made of rows of blanks, pages that are only photos of paper, too big for an upload form – and each one is said in plain words, with a button that opens the tool that fixes it. It also says what it checked and found fine. Checking changes nothing. It looks at the file itself, not a screenshot: a picture of a problem cannot be read reliably on a phone.

                        Choose a file. A PDF uses the page reader the other PDF tools here use, downloaded once.

                          Explain it simply

                          What happensThe hard words in the file are found and each one is explained. If the file is a court order or judgment, it also says who is who, quotes the sentences that look like the decision and every time limit, each with its page, and never says who won: ask a lawyer before you act on it. The meaning comes from the file itself first – where it says what a word means, or spells out a short form – shown in its own words with the page. Otherwise it comes from a checked list of about two hundred admission, form, money, legal and medical words, each written and then checked by Claude. A word in neither is not explained, and never guessed: a small AI was tried for this on a real admission notice and gave confident wrong meanings, so none is used. You can also type any word to look it up. Nothing is sent anywhere.

                          Choose a file, or just type a word below. A PDF uses the page reader the other PDF tools here use, downloaded once.

                          What am I signing?

                          What happensThe paper is read on this phone. If it is a contract (a rental agreement, a loan, an insurance policy, a job offer), the sentences that catch people out are marked: a lock-in, a penalty, renewing by itself, interest and late fees, a promise not to work elsewhere, the other side changing the terms, things not covered, giving up your rights. Each is shown in the paper’s own sentence, with its page and why it matters, next to every amount, percentage, time and date in it. It never says a clause is illegal or unfair, and it is not legal advice: read the marked clauses twice and ask a lawyer before you sign. Nothing is sent anywhere.

                          Choose the paper you are about to sign. A scan or a photo is a picture of words and cannot be read here.

                          Read a prescription

                          What happensA typed or printed prescription or hospital discharge summary is read line by line. Each medicine is shown exactly as written: its name, strength, form and dosing, with short forms like 1-0-1, BD or SOS said in plain words, never changed or completed. The generic (salt) name is given only when the prescription itself prints it. Where the medicine and its strength match (when the salt is not written, only as a possible match the pharmacist must confirm), it also shows the heading the government’s essential-medicines list files it under and the cheaper Jan Aushadhi product and price. It gives no advice on doses, no warnings about mixing medicines and no diagnosis: ask your doctor or pharmacist before you change or stop anything. It cannot read handwriting. Nothing is sent anywhere.

                          Choose the prescription. A photo of one, or handwriting, cannot be read here.

                          Explain a bill

                          What happensA household bill (electricity, phone, water, gas, hospital) is read on this phone. It shows the amount due, the due date, the bill period and the account number, each copied from beside its own label with its page, then every line with a plain meaning where a checked list has one, whether the lines add up to the total, and what to check: arrears, a late fee, a one-time charge, a line printed twice, a mention of disconnection. Nothing is guessed or worked out beyond adding the lines. If a number looks wrong, ask the office that sent the bill. Nothing is sent anywhere.

                          Choose the bill. A scan or a photo of a bill is a picture and cannot be read here.

                          Admission paperwork helper

                          What happensTap your answers. The papers, copies, attestation, affidavits and stamp paper that the KEA, MCC and Mysore Medical College notices ask for are listed, and every line names the notice it came from (its name, year, page and a short quote). Where a notice is silent, the line says “the notice does not say”: nothing is guessed. Attestation (a stamp from a gazetted officer or a notary that says a copy is a true copy) is part of the list. Nothing you tap leaves this phone. Confirm with the college’s own admission office before you go: these notices can be revised.

                          Answer the questions above, then tap Make my checklist.

                          School circulars, explained

                          What happensA school or board notice is read on this phone. It shows the subject line as written, who it is for, every date and deadline, every amount of money, what to do or bring, and whom to contact, each in the notice’s own words with its page. Nothing is reworded or guessed. A file that is not a notice shows nothing. Check every date and amount against the notice itself.

                          Choose the notice. A scan or a photo of a notice is a picture and cannot be read here.

                          Kids’ reader

                          What happensPaste a text, or choose a PDF, Word or text file. It is laid out in big type, a few sentences to a page, and a heading starts a new page. A word that is not on a list of everyday English words gets a dotted line and is listed at the foot of its page as “ask a grown-up”. That means only “not on the list”: an easy word can be marked and a hard one can be missed. It does not add pictures, does not explain any word and changes none of the words. It works on this phone; nothing is sent anywhere.

                          Every exam website’s rules

                          What happensThe photo and signature limits this app knows, each read from the official notice named under it. To use one, open Photo for a form and pick it in its list. Rules change every year: check your own exam’s latest notice before you submit.

                            RTI application maker

                            What happensThe RTI (Right to Information) is your right to ask a government office for its papers. Tap Explain the RTI to read the law in plain words, each fact beside the words of the law it comes from. Then fill in the boxes: the application is checked (the fee, the 500-word limit) and set out properly for you to print or send. It follows the central rules; a State office has its own rules, and the page says so. This is a guide, not legal advice. Nothing you type leaves this phone.

                            Fill in the boxes above, then tap Make my application.

                            
      
                            
    
                            
  
                            

  
                            
    
                            Patient leaflet
                            
    
                            What happensYou type or paste a paragraph of advice in English. A translation program (a model called IndicTrans2) runs on this phone and writes it in Hindi or Kannada, one sentence at a time, with your English beside it. It is a draft, never the finished leaflet: a machine can drop a small word such as “not” or “if” and the sentence still looks fine. Every number is compared automatically, but nothing else is, so a doctor or pharmacist must check the whole translation before anyone acts on it. Your text never leaves this phone; only the program itself is downloaded, once each time you open this page.

                                Bills to one Excel list
                                
    
                                What happensChoose your suppliers’ bills: many PDFs, or one PDF holding many bills. Each bill becomes one row: the seller’s GSTIN, bill number, date, taxable value, CGST, SGST, IGST, cess and total. Every figure is taken from beside its own label on the bill; one it could not find is left empty and yellow, never made up or set to zero. Each GSTIN is checked with its own check letter, and each bill’s tax is added up against its total; a row that does not add up says by how much. The same bill twice (Original and Duplicate copies) is listed once. A second sheet says where every figure was found. A scanned bill is read with text recognition, which can misread the rupee sign as a 7: the sums check points to those rows. Everything happens here on this phone; the reading tools (about 30 MB) download once. A GSTR-2B statement does not need this: the GST portal’s own “Download GSTR-2B summary (Excel)” button gives it already.
                                
    
    
                                
      
    
                                
    
                                
      
    
                                
    
                                
    
                                  
  
                                  

  
                                  
    
                                  Is this book free?
                                  
    
                                  What happensType a book’s name. You get, for each book that matches: free, legally – and where – or the shops to buy it from, or that no free copy was found. Legal copies only: a copy counts as free only when Open Library lets anyone read it, when Project Gutenberg or Standard Ebooks publish it, when Wikidata records the whole book at an address, or when Google Books shows every page. A library that lends a scan is not counted as free. A price is shown only when a shop’s own list gave it; otherwise the shops are links and it says the price was not checked. Only the name you type is sent – to Open Library, Wikidata and Google Books (plus your own Google Books key, if you add one, to Google Books only). No file goes anywhere.
                                  
    
    
    
                                  Your own Google Books key (optional)
      
                                  Without a key, Google often answers “busy” and prices say “not checked”. A free key from your own Google account (Google Cloud console, Books API) fixes that. It is sent only to Google Books, with each look-up.
                                  
      
      
      
    
                                  
    
                                  
      
    
                                  
    
                                  
    
                                  
  
                                  

  
                                  
    
                                  Book reader
                                  
    
                                  What happensThe file is laid out to read: plain paragraphs sized for the phone, a map of its chapters, a search box, and the page each part is on. Every hard word has a dotted line: tap it for its meaning, which comes from the file itself first, then from this book’s word list if you add one (written and checked by Claude for that one book), else from a checked list. A word in none of these is left plain, never guessed. Tables and pictures are not shown, and the reader says at the top which pages had them. Saved, it is one page that opens in any browser with no internet. Nothing is sent anywhere, unless you make a word list with a free AI below and tick the box that sends the book for it.
                                  
    
    
    
                                  
    
                                  
      No word list? Make one with a free AI (needs a free key)
      
                                  The book is read in parts by a free Google Gemini model, which lists every term, name, idiom and working word a newcomer would not know, with what it is, why this book uses it and what you can learn. A second model then checks every entry against a sentence of the book. It is the same method, and the same instructions, as the lists Claude makes, with a smaller free model: measured on HPMOR, it found about 72% of a hand-made list; Claude found 93%. A long book takes about 20 of the free calls and some minutes; if the page is closed part-way, every answer so far is kept on this phone and the next try carries on.
                                  
      
                                  
        
        
        
      
                                  
      
                                  
        
        
      
                                  
      
                                  A free Gemini key: aistudio.google.com/apikey (a Google account, no card). A free Groq key: console.groq.com/keys. With a Groq key the check is done by a larger model: on HPMOR it corrected 75 entries the Gemini check let through. The free Gemini limit is about 20 calls a day for each model; it resets at 12:30 pm India time.
                                  
      
                                  The key is yours, and so are its terms. Google and Groq allow a key only to people aged 18 or over who accept their terms (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms, console.groq.com/docs/legal). This app only passes your key to them from your phone; it is not their service and does not see what they send back anywhere but here.
                                  
      
      
                                  
      
                                  
    
                                  
    
                                  A PDF uses the page reader the other PDF tools here use, downloaded once.
                                  
    
                                  
      
                                  
      
      
                                  
    
                                  
  
                                  

  
                                  
    
                                  WhatsApp chat as a book
                                  
    
                                  What happensYour exported chat becomes a book to read, in the same reader as the Book reader: a map with a chapter for each month and each day inside it, a search box, and every message as it was exported. Nothing is added and nothing is guessed about what anyone meant. In WhatsApp: open the chat, More, Export chat, Without media, then choose that .txt file here.
                                  
    
    
                                  
    
                                  
    
                                  
      
                                  
      
                                    
      
      
                                    
      
                                    
    
                                    
  
                                    

  
                                    
    
                                    Web page as a book
                                    
    
                                    What happensA web page you saved becomes a clean book to read offline, in the same reader as the Book reader: only the article, with the menus, cookie banners, adverts, related stories and comments left out. It says at the top what it left out. Nothing is fetched from the internet: save the page first (in Chrome: the menu, Save page as, “Webpage, Single File” or “Webpage, HTML Only”), then choose it here.
                                    
    
    
                                    
    
                                    
      
                                    
      
                                      
      
      
                                      
      
                                      
    
                                      
  
                                      

  
                                      
    0
    network requests since you opened a file. Your file is read and rebuilt on this device only.
  
                                      

  
                                      
    Words used on this page
    
                                      
      
                                      PDF
                                      A file that looks the same on every phone and printer. Most forms and affidavits are PDFs.
                                      
      
                                      A4, A3, A5
                                      Paper sizes. A4 is 210 × 297 mm, the normal Indian office sheet. A3 is two A4s side by side; A5 is half an A4. All share the same shape, so shrinking A3 to A4 loses nothing.
                                      
      
                                      Letter, Legal
                                      American sizes. Legal (216 × 356 mm) is taller than A4, which is why converted documents often refuse to print on A4.
                                      
      
                                      Booklet
                                      Sheets printed on both sides, stacked and folded in the middle, like a small book. Page 1 and the last page land on the same side of the outer sheet, so the pages must be printed out of order; this page works that order out.
                                      
      
                                      Signature
                                      A printer's word for one folded bundle of sheets. A thick book is several signatures stacked, because more than about 15 sheets will not fold flat. This page calls them "booklets".
                                      
      
                                      Binding margin (gutter)
                                      Extra blank space on the edge of the page that gets bound - by staples on the side, a spiral or a file - so the binding never covers the words. Printed on both sides, the back of each sheet is bound on its right-hand edge, so its margin moves to the right.
                                      
      
                                      Creep
                                      When a stack of sheets is folded, the inner sheets have to go round the outer ones, so they stick out a little at the open edge (about 0.1 mm per sheet for office paper). Correcting for creep moves those pages towards the fold by the same amount, so the margins match.
                                      
      
                                      Page edges (finding them)
                                      The Scan tab looks for the biggest bright, four-sided patch in the photo and puts the corners there. It only does this when it is sure; on a white desk, or when the page fills the whole photo, it leaves the corners for you to drag.
                                      
      
                                      Flip on short edge
                                      A printer setting for two-sided printing on a sideways sheet: the back is printed so it reads the right way up after you turn the sheet over along its short side. The other choice, long edge, prints every back upside down for a booklet.
                                      
      
                                      Portrait / landscape
                                      Upright / sideways.
                                      
      
                                      KB
                                      Kilobyte, a measure of file size. 1000 KB is about 1 MB. Exam portals often say "photo under 50 KB".
                                      
      
                                      px
                                      Pixel, one dot of a photo. "200 × 230 px" means 200 dots wide, 230 tall.
                                      
      
                                      Scan
                                      Here: a phone photo of a paper page, turned into a flat, clean page as if it had gone through a scanner.
                                      
      
                                      Straighten
                                      A page photographed at an angle looks like a slanted shape. Placing its four corners lets the page stretch it back into a true rectangle.
                                      
      
                                      Ink saver
                                      Printing a grey photo of a page wastes toner on the grey. Turning the paper white and the writing pure black uses ink only where there are words.
                                      
      
                                      Crop
                                      Cutting a photo down to the part you keep. The dashed frame shows exactly the part that will be saved.
                                      
      
                                      Face guide
                                      A dashed oval drawn over the preview to show how big the face should be. Exams reject photos where the face is a small dot in a big background. The oval is only on the screen, never in the saved photo.
                                      
      
                                      White background
                                      Portals reject photos with a room, wall or pattern behind the person. This option finds where the person ends and paints everything else white, keeping fine hair at the edges. Your face and clothes are left exactly as they were.
                                      
      
                                      Background colour
                                      Most exam portals ask for white. A few notices ask for off-white, light blue or light grey instead; pick one of those only when your notice says so. Changing it does not run the model again, so it is instant.
                                      
      
                                      Touch-up brush
                                      After the background is made plain, a finger on the preview can paint "keep this" (hair or a shoulder that vanished) or "remove this" (a chair or flag that survived). It changes only the model's map of where the person is; your photo's own pixels are never painted.
                                      
      
                                      Model
                                      Here: a small program trained on many photos to tell a person from what is behind them. It runs inside this page on your own phone, which is why the photo never has to be uploaded. This one is MODNet (free, Apache-2.0 licence).
                                      
      
                                      Zoom
                                      Enlarging the photo inside the frame, so the face fills more of it.
                                      
      
                                      DPI
                                      Dots per inch: how many pixels make one inch when printed. At 200 DPI, 3 cm is about 240 pixels.
                                      
      
                                      Preset
                                      Numbers already filled in for one exam, copied from that exam's official notice. The note under it names which notice.
                                      
      
                                      JPG
                                      The usual photo format. It gets smaller by dropping detail the eye barely notices.
                                      
      
                                      PNG
                                      A picture format that keeps every pixel exactly and can have see-through parts. Files are bigger than JPG.
                                      
      
                                      WEBP
                                      A newer picture format from Google: smaller than JPG at the same sharpness, and it can keep every pixel. A few older websites do not accept it.
                                      
      
                                      Format
                                      The kind of file, shown by the ending of its name (.jpg, .png, .pdf). Changing the format rewrites the file in another kind; the picture should look the same.
                                      
      
                                      Text recognition
                                      A program that looks at a picture of words and works out which letters they are, the way you read a sign. It can misread a blurred or tiny letter, so it also says how sure it was of each word; the words it was unsure of are marked for you to check. (Its technical name is OCR, optical character recognition.)
                                      
      
                                      Screenshot
                                      A picture of what was on the screen, taken by the phone itself. The words in it are only dots of colour until they are read back out.
                                      
      
                                      .txt
                                      A file of plain words and nothing else: no bold, no pictures. Every phone and computer opens it.
                                      
      
                                      PowerPoint
                                      Microsoft’s program for making slides: the pages shown on a screen behind someone giving a talk.
                                      
      
                                      Handout
                                      Printed pages that go with a talk, so listeners can follow and write on them. Here: each slide’s words and its speaker notes, one after another.
                                      
      
                                      Speaker notes
                                      What the person giving the talk wrote under each slide for themselves: the audience never sees them on the screen. PowerPoint keeps them in the same file as the slides.
                                      
      
                                      .pptx
                                      A PowerPoint file: a set of slides. Google Slides, Keynote and WPS open it too. (The older .ppt kind must be turned into .pptx first.)
                                      
      
                                      Hidden slide
                                      A slide the author kept in the file but told PowerPoint to skip when showing and printing. It is left out here in the same way.
                                      
      
                                      .zip
                                      One file that holds several files packed together. Phones open it in the Files app and show the pictures inside.
                                      
      
                                      EXIF
                                      Hidden notes a camera writes inside a photo: which way up it was held, the date, the phone model, sometimes the place. Changing the format here keeps the photo upright and does not copy these notes.
                                      
      
                                      .docx
                                      A Word file. When a PDF is turned into Word, each printed line can become its own paragraph and the spacing becomes rows of spaces, which is why pressing Backspace makes whole lines jump.
                                      
      
                                      OpenDocument
                                      The free file kinds made by LibreOffice and Google Docs’ “download as”: .odt is a text file (like Word), .odp is slides (like PowerPoint), .ods is a sheet (like Excel). Inside, like a .docx, it is a .zip of parts, and its pictures are kept as their own files.
                                      
      
                                      Linked picture
                                      A picture a file only points to, by its internet or disk address, instead of carrying it inside. The file shows it only while that address still works. It cannot be taken out of the file, because it was never in it; fetching it would tell that address you opened the file, so it is counted and never fetched.
                                      
      
                                      Fake gap
                                      Spaces or tabs a converter inserted to copy the look of the PDF. They look like normal spacing until you edit.
                                      
      
                                      Voice note
                                      The recording WhatsApp makes when you hold the microphone button. It is not an MP3: it is Opus inside an .opus or .ogg file, and some websites, older players and upload forms refuse it.
                                      
      
                                      MP3
                                      The oldest widely used way of squeezing sound into a small file. Nothing plays MP3 badly, which is the only reason to use it: every phone, website, car stereo and upload form accepts one.
                                      
      
                                      Opus
                                      A newer, cleverer way of squeezing sound, made for speech over the internet. It sounds as good as MP3 at about a quarter of the size — which is why an MP3 made from a voice note is usually several times bigger than the voice note was. The sound is the same; only the file is bigger.
                                      
      
                                      AAC
                                      What iPhone voice memos, Android recordings and the sound inside most videos are. Newer than MP3, smaller at the same quality, and accepted almost as widely.
                                      
      
                                      FLAC
                                      Sound squeezed with nothing at all thrown away, like a .zip for music. Big files, perfect copies.
                                      
      
                                      Lossy
                                      A way of making a file smaller by throwing away detail a person is unlikely to notice. MP3, Opus and AAC are all lossy, so an MP3 can never be compared with its original sample by sample — only by whether it still sounds the same, which is what this page checks.
                                      
      
                                      Samples a second
                                      How many times a second the sound was measured when it was recorded (also called the sample rate). 44,100 is a CD; 48,000 is a phone or a video; 16,000 is plenty for speech. It sets the highest note the recording can hold — half the rate, and no more.
                                      
      
                                      kbps
                                      Kilobits per second: how much room the sound is given each second. More means a bigger file and finer detail. A voice note spends about 24 kbps; music wants 128 or more. This page picks the number from what the recording actually carries, so it never spends 128 kbps storing silence.
                                      
      
                                      Mono, stereo
                                      One channel of sound, or two (left and right). A voice note is mono. A recording that arrives mono stays mono — making it stereo would double the size and add nothing.
                                      
      
                                      Played back to check it
                                      After the MP3 is written it is opened again and compared with your original: the same length, the same loudness, the loud and quiet parts in the same places, and the same highest note. If any of those has moved, the MP3 is thrown away and the page says what was wrong instead of handing you a bad file.
                                      
      
                                      Network request
                                      Any time a page talks to the internet. Zero after you pick a file means nothing about the file was sent anywhere. Ticking White background, or tapping "Make it fit anyway" on a PDF, makes the page download that tool once; the counter still counts those downloads and names them, so nothing is hidden.
                                      
    
                                      
  
                                      
  
                                      
    Licences and privacy
    
                                      What this page collects: nothing reaches us - there is no server of ours, no account, no sign-in, no analytics, no tracking and no advert. Your files are read and rebuilt on this phone and are not uploaded; the only two tools that send anything you give them are named below, and each asks first.
                                      
    
                                      What stays on this phone, in this browser only: the details you save in Your details (which can include an Aadhaar number, kept as plain text in the browser until you tap Forget them); AI keys, only if you tick remember; word lists made for a book (Forget the saved word lists); your reading place and text size in the Book reader; and the speech model once downloaded. Clearing this site's data in your browser removes all of it. Your files themselves are never stored.
                                      
    
                                      When it talks to the internet, and the counter above names every one: opening the single-file copy fetches nothing, because its fonts and its PDF and zip helpers (pdf-lib, JSZip) are inside it (the development copy, web/filer.html, loads those two from cdnjs each time it opens); the first time a tool needs a bigger helper (a PDF reader, the text recogniser, a small model) it is downloaded from jsDelivr, cdnjs, PyPI (files.pythonhosted.org) or Hugging Face, with nothing from your file. Two tools send something you give them: Is this book free? sends the book title you type to Open Library, Wikidata and Google Books (and your own Google Books key, only if you paste one, to Google Books alone); Book words sends parts of the book's text to Google Gemini or Groq, only with a key you paste in yourself and only after you tick "Yes, send this book's text" for that book. Those services' own privacy policies then apply. The microphone is used only when you tap Start the microphone. The full privacy policy is in privacy.html beside this app.
                                      
    
                                      Health tools (prescription, lab report, medicine leaflet) give general information only. They are not a medical device and not medical advice: ask your doctor or pharmacist before you start, stop or change anything.
                                      
    
                                      No warranty. This app is free and comes as it is, with no warranty. Keep a copy of any file before you change it, and check every result before you rely on it, submit it or send it. Tools that explain or fill forms, notices and official documents give general information, not legal advice, and are not connected with any government body, court, college or company they name. The full terms are in LICENSE.txt beside this app.
